rounds.text: Aryaman Capital Markets Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at a modest P/E of 14.9 despite exceptional capital efficiency and explosive profit growth [E1, E19]. The company boasts a phenomenal return on equity of 30.0% and a return on capital employed of 32.0%, both vastly outperforming sector benchmarks where ROCE sits at a mere 6.1% [E12, E13, E65]. Profitability has scaled dramatically with a 5-year compounded profit growth of 157% and a 3-year growth of 165%, while fundamentals have decisively outpaced recent price action [E19, E20, E45]. Furthermore, operational quality is pristine: the business is completely debt-free with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x, operating cash flows of Rs 34 Cr fully back reported profits with a 1.21x cash conversion, and working capital requirements have contracted sharply from 88.2 days to 35.6 days [E34, E35, E37, E53]. A discounted cash flow model suggests a deep margin of safety of 63.5%, with the current share price implying a mere 4.1% earnings growth against a much higher base-case trajectory [E43, E44]. Conceded: the company has delivered a poor sales growth of -14.5% over the past five years and offers a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4, E55].

While profitability metrics appear robust, the business suffers from a pronounced contraction in top-line growth over medium and short time horizons, evidenced by compounded sales growth of -15% over five years and an alarming -38% over the trailing twelve months [E15, E17]. Furthermore, the stock trades at a valuation premium over its sector across key multiples, specifically commanding a price-to-earnings ratio of 21.24x against a sector benchmark of 18.62x and a price-to-book ratio of 4.83x compared to a meager 1.26x sector benchmark [E6, E7]. Shareholder returns are further compromised by a complete lack of capital return, as demonstrated by a dividend yield of 0.00% despite the company reporting repeated profits [E4, E54]. Conceded: [E19]. Price action also reflects underlying fatigue, with the share price contracting by -16% over the past year while sitting merely 38% of the way up its 52-week range [E5, E25]. Finally, institutional interest remains entirely flat with a neutral money flow signal [E41].

While the bear highlights top-line contraction over the 5-year and trailing twelve month periods [E15, E17], it ignores the longer-term 10-year sales expansion of 20% [E14] and the impressive quarterly sales surge of +110% YoY captured in the recent screening metrics [E57]. The bear's selected P/E multiple of 21.24x [E6] relies on a specific data provider rather than the filed statement P/E of 14.9x [E1], which presents a much more modest valuation for a company generating a phenomenal 31.43% ROCE against a sector benchmark of just 5.86% [E10]. Conceded: the 0.00% dividend yield [E4], though this retention directly fuels outstanding wealth-compounding efficiency, as seen in the 157% 5-year profit growth [E19] and an elite ROE of 25.71% that vastly outperforms the 5.57% sector benchmark [E9]. The bear points to a 16% 1-year share price drop [E25] and neutral institutional flow [E41], but this disconnect ignores the fundamental reality that profits have vastly outpaced price action, leaving the stock trading at a massive discount to its discounted cash flow intrinsic value with a 63.5% margin of safety [E42, E43, E45]. Finally, the bear's concern over share price fatigue overlooks the pristine balance sheet featuring zero debt [E37, E38] and an extraordinary cash conversion rate of 1.21x where profits are fully backed by actual cash [E34].

Conceded: the 10-year sales expansion of 20% [E14] and the cash conversion of 1.21x where profits are fully backed by actual cash [E34]. However, the bull's dismissal of top-line contraction is contradicted by a severe 5-year compounded sales drop of -15% and a trailing twelve month sales collapse of -38% [E15, E17]. Conceded: the filed statement P/E of 14.9x [E1]. Even so, the alternative P/E of 21.24x sits above the sector benchmark of 18.62x, and the price-to-book ratio of 4.83x heavily exceeds the sector benchmark of 1.26x [E6, E7]. The bull points to a discounted cash flow intrinsic value and a 63.5% margin of safety [E42, E43], but completely ignores that the dividend yield remains at 0.00% and the stock price has fallen 16% over the past year [E4, E25]. Finally, the bull cites strong quarterly sales surges [E57], yet the record shows the company has delivered a poor sales growth of -14.5% over the past five years alongside zero dividend payouts despite repeated profits [E54, E55].
